newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PGM market seen tight despite Russian sales.
newsitem.headline: Japan PGM market seen tight despite Russian sales.

text.p: Japan's physical market for platinum group metals (PGM), especially palladium, has stayed tight and is expected to remain so for the next two months despite the long-awaited resumption of Russian PGM exports in July, traders said on Monday.
Even the August PGM deliveries that Japanese traders expect to receive in the early part of this month are unlikely to alleviate the tightness significantly, they said.
"Most PGM imports for August will go straight to end-users. There would be little available metal to allay the overheated yen-based PGM market," an official at a major bullion house said.
It is not clear at this stage when Japan will receive contracted August PGM shipments from Russia, but some traders are expecting them to arrive later this week.
Traders said, however, that Japan's physical platinum market has not been as tight as the palladium market, due partly to lacklustre platinum demand from the jewellery sector.

Platinum premiums in Japan are now quoted around $1.80 to $2.00 per ounce over the Zurich benchmark, while palladium premiums are around $7 to $8 per ounce. The normal premium for both metals is $1.00 to $1.50.

Traders expected Japan's PGM imports for July, when Russia resumed contracted shipments to Japan, to rise slightly from June, although they may be slightly lower than the same month a year earlier, they said.
Some traders estimated Japan's palladium imports for July at about six tonnes, compared with 5.75 tonnes in June and 6.66 tonnes in the same month last year.
July platinum imports are expected to be about 4.0 to 4.5 tonnes, against 3.38 tonnes in June and 6.92 tonnes in July 1996.

Japanese traders blamed the recent steep rise in PGM prices on an abnormally large overhang of short palladium positions on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) and lingering uncertainty over the stability of Russian supplies.

"Private investors (on TOCOM), who face large losses, have just started to cover their shorts. The bullish trend will not end until that covering gets close to completion," a trader at a major trading house said.
He pegged the next resistance level for palladium at $250 per ounce and for platinum at $450 per ounce.

As for Japanese demand, although the sharp price increases have dampened overall PGM demand, especially after palladium rose above $200 per ounce, some end-users who have delayed covering their requirements are eager to buy the metals, market sources said.

"It would be inevitable for the electronics industry to continue its efforts to shift to cheaper metals like nickel from palladium, which would pressure demand in the longer term," another official of a major bullion house said.
